mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary policy, reducing discount rates for equity valuations and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate exceeding 5.5% indicates economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE exceeds 5.5%, SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals strong consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint increase in HOUST and RSAFS (both > 0.5% MoM) does not produce positive 60-day SPX returns in at least 60% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles, rising federal funds rates compress equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: During periods when FEDFUNDS rises at > 0.25% per month, SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases over a 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Strong housing starts (HOUST) growth indicates robust consumer demand, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST growth does not correlate with positive 5-day SPX returns in more than 55% of cases over a 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Sluggish job growth (PAYEMS growth < 0.2% YoY) signals economic deceleration, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS growth is below 0.2% YoY, SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases over a 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% YoY) triggers monetary policy tightening expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL is above 3.0% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in industrial production (INDPRO) and decline in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a strengthening economy, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO increases by > 0.3% MoM and UNRATE decreases by > 0.1pp, SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of cases over a 3-year window.
